body.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_N\) with \(\mu_D>0\), \[E_{P_T}[Y_T(1,D_T(1))-Y_T(0,D_T(0))\mid D_T(1)>D_T(0)]=\theta_T=\frac{\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_T(x)\delta_Y(x)}{\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_T(x)\delta_D(x)},\] and every cell contrast is identified from each source covering that cell.
body.justification: This links the statistical ratio to the target causal effect among compliers.
body.gap: Dahabreh et al., Theorem 1, identify target potential-outcome means under their baseline conditions; Theorems 2 and 3 give weaker collection-positivity routes, with Theorem 3 using the cell-specific trial subsets of Section 3.4.2. They do not identify or analyze a weakly identified noncompliance ratio. Rudolph and van der Laan use receipt observed in the target site for their CACE first stage, whereas the novel compliance-ITT transport condition here assembles that first stage from covering source trials.
body.consumer: The five-site Moving to Opportunity analysis can use different trials to supply different target cells.
